notes:
As touchless interactions become part of everyday life, we invite people into a world of touch and human connection through Samsung’s digital interfaces.
Through SmartThings, Samsung connects smartphones, home appliances and TVs. 
Our retail proposal extends these connections between devices into connections between people.
Visitors can try Samsung products firsthand and feel the textures of the materials used in the products and throughout the store. 
By exploring and using the products together, they can discover one another’s ways of living and personal preferences.
We propose a retail store where Samsung products bring people together—a shared interface for human connection.

We saw a parallel between weaving and the way Samsung connects people and technology to shape everyday living environments. Just as the arrangement and combination of threads create fabrics with different patterns, Samsung’s technology helps shape living environments that reflect each person’s preferences and way of life.

Weaving combines thread colours, materials and structures to create different textures and patterns. We considered how Samsung’s technology is experienced when people see and touch its products. Reading information on a screen and feeling the texture of a surface are different experiences. In this retail space, we wanted visitors to explore the products’ features while also feeling the textures around them. The fabric used on The Premiere became our starting point.

Samsung’s ultra-short-throw projector, The Premiere, uses Kvadrat fabric to blend naturally with living-room furniture. By bringing a material also used on sofas and chairs onto the product, Samsung considered both the atmosphere of the room and the texture people would feel.
Because this fabric also covers the built-in speaker, it needed to retain its furniture-like texture while allowing sound to pass through.

A tight weave could affect sound quality, so Samsung developed a new woven structure with more space between the threads. This allows sound to pass through while preserving the fabric’s appearance.
The same surface serves as a finish that fits into the home and a structure designed for acoustic performance.
We carry this approach into the space: designing materials and technology together, with people’s everyday lives in mind.

We also expressed this design approach through the space’s graphics. Samsung’s “Design Is an Act of Love” takes the form of a heart, while weaving is represented by two interlaced threads.
The threads carry two meanings: the coming together of humanism and high tech, and the connection between people with their own distinct tastes and ways of living.
Each thread retains its colour as they form a single heart, expressing togetherness that preserves individuality.

A table is an everyday place where people sit face to face, eat, talk and spend time doing things together. Each person has their own seat, yet they share one surface—an expression of people with distinct tastes coming together.
We bring this meaning into a space where people use Samsung products together. Visitors can share photos on a Galaxy phone or watch TV at the same table, starting conversations and discovering each other’s preferences.
Fabric is applied to the table surfaces their hands naturally touch. They experience Samsung’s technology through images and sound, while feeling the material’s texture with their hands. By bringing these experiences together in one place, we aim to make Samsung’s design something people can understand through their senses.

We applied the diagonal pattern of the weave to the walls and central table. Repeated surfaces bend at the same angle, creating routes to walk through and places to sit between them.
The central table forms one continuous surface for using a range of Samsung products together. The surrounding seats face the table, so each individual place opens towards the shared centre.

Visitors enter a space framed by angled surfaces and immerse themselves in an atmosphere distinct from everyday life.
The zigzag structure partially conceals the interior, inviting them to move further in and discover what lies beyond.
Around each corner, Samsung products and new places to pause come into view. Visitors move closer to try the products and feel the texture of the fabric on the surfaces they touch.
At the table, they sit across from others, looking at or using the same products and sharing a conversation.
The space is designed to let curiosity lead to hands-on exploration, and shared experiences create opportunities for people to connect.

We propose a wooden lattice ceiling with integrated lighting and herringbone wood flooring. The diagonal patterns above and below create a consistent visual rhythm throughout the space.
The walls combine colors drawn from Bespoke panels with textile textures, while their three-dimensional surfaces catch light and cast shadows.
For the central table, we propose a fabric finish inspired by the textile used on The Premiere.

This concludes our proposal for a Samsung retail store as an interface that connects people.
Thank you.
